taxonomy.subtopic: Reversible competitive antagonism and surmountable rightward dose-response shift

questions.stem_html: Investigators measure the response of isolated vascular smooth muscle to increasing concentrations of an agonist. They repeat the experiment after adding a fixed concentration of compound X. The second concentration-response curve is shifted to the right in parallel, but reaches the same maximal response as the control curve. Which property of compound X best explains this finding?

options.text_html: It blocks a downstream signaling protein in a noncompetitive manner
It accelerates degradation of the agonist before receptor binding
It is a partial agonist with lower intrinsic efficacy than the full agonist
It reversibly competes with the agonist for the same receptor-binding site
It irreversibly reduces the number of functional receptors

questions.explanation_html: A reversible competitive antagonist occupies the same orthosteric site as the agonist. A higher agonist concentration can overcome the antagonist, so the agonist EC50 increases and the curve shifts rightward while Emax is preserved. The antagonism is therefore surmountable.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Irreversible loss of functional receptors generally lowers the maximal achievable response once receptor reserve is exhausted.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: A partial agonist can reduce the response to a full agonist when both are present and does not characteristically produce a simple parallel shift with preserved Emax in all systems.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: A noncompetitive block downstream from the receptor decreases efficacy and therefore tends to lower Emax.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Faster agonist degradation could alter exposure, but the classic parallel rightward shift with preserved Emax identifies reversible competitive receptor antagonism.

questions.educational_objective: Reversible competitive antagonists increase the agonist concentration required for a given effect, causing a parallel rightward shift with increased EC50 and unchanged Emax.

media.alt_text: Original graded dose-response graph showing a parallel rightward shift in the presence of a reversible competitive antagonist while maximal response is preserved.
